text:
infra-bot: ALERT: elevated page_migration rate on pool24/card7 (node gpu-24-7). row_remap counter increasing, page_retire events observed. auto-threshold breached at 3/5. :eyes:
anya: saw this earlier this morning, thanks for the ping. how bad is the trend?
maria: looks like a sustained uptick over 24h, sharp jump ~08:10 UTC. raw metrics attached to the alert.
leo: any Xid errors correlating? those usually precede a hard failure here.
anya: checking logs now, grepping syslog for Xid and page_retire.
anya: ```
Mar 18 08:09:52 gpu-24-7 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 31, PID=2345, GPU UUID=GPU-abc123
Mar 18 08:10:01 gpu-24-7 nvlink: page_migration: row_remap_inc=4, page_retire_inc=2
Mar 18 08:10:20 gpu-24-7 hwmon: ECC correctable errors rising on channel 2
```
ryan: that Xid 31 + row_remap increments is textbook for imminent page retirement progression. recommend draining before instance hits critical.
sre-oncall: planned drain ok? pool24 is low utilization today but we have two training jobs that might be impacted.
leo: which nodes are affected in pool24? single card or multiple?
maria: current alert only for gpu-24-7 but we see smaller upticks on gpu-24-3 and gpu-24-9 (row_remap rate ~0.4/hr). trend suggests propagation.
anya: suggested triage steps: 1) cordon node gpu-24-7 2) migrate pods / jobs 3) run nvdiag and memtest_long on the card 4) if row_remap counter keeps climbing, schedule replacement and RMA.
chipops: agree. also check if pool autoscaler can temporarily spin up replacement capacity to avoid evictions. cost hit small, but better than job failures.
ryan: command to cordon and drain (k8s): `kubectl cordon gpu-24-7 && kubectl drain gpu-24-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`
sre-oncall: starting cordon+drain now, migrating 2 jobs (train-vision-17, batch-embed-3). ETA ~6m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
infra-bot: ACTION: node gpu-24-7 cordoned by sre-oncall at 2026-03-18T08:15:30Z
anya: after pods clear, I'll run quick memtest and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.err.corrected,utilization.gpu,row_remap_counters --format=csv` to capture snapshot.
anya: snapshot: ```memory.err.corrected [count] : 134
utilization.gpu [%] : 2
row_remap_counters : 7
```
leo: 134 corrected ECC is not huge by itself, but combined with row_remap growth and Xid it's concerning. recommend immediate RMA candidate.
maria: filing ticket INFRA-7891 with logs + diag, tag warranty. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-7891
chipops: note: check spare pool inventory before we mark for offline replacement. if low, we may want temporary capacity in us-west-1 instead of full replacement next week.
ryan: short-term: keep node cordoned, mark GPU as degraded in pool allocator so scheduler avoids it, then enqueue RMA. long-term: add alert to detect Xid+row_remap joint pattern (currently we only alert on page_migration rate).
sre-oncall: done migrating jobs, memtest queued (30m run). streaming logs to ticket.
anya: after memtest finishes, if errors persist we'll remove card from service and swap next maintenance window.
leo: +1. please also escalate to vendor with full logs (Xid 31 trace, row_remap counters, ECC timeseries). chipops can coordinate RMA.
chipops: ack, will open vendor case with INFRA-7891 attachments and SLA request.
infra-bot: NOTE: automated watch created for pool24 with increased sampling frequency for row_remap and ECC metrics.
anya: follow-up: set a reminder for 48h to check propagation across pool24. if more nodes show similar pattern, we may need a preemptive replacement plan.
maria: agreed. I'll add a short postmortem stub to the ticket after vendor response.
ryan: thanks everyone. leaving cordon; do not uncordon until chipops/RMA confirm or node passes extended memtest.
leo: adding `--degraded` tag to the pool inventory for gpu-24-7 so it's clear in dashboards. :white_check_mark:
